title: Product of basis functions
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $I$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\{b_i:i\in I\}$ is a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$, with $b_{i_0}$ the constant-one function for some $i_0\in I$, and orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$. For a natural number $n$, a multi-index $a$ of length $n$ with values in $I$, and $x\in\Omega^n$, the corresponding product function is $\prod_{j=0}^{n-1} b_{a(j)}(x(j))$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function basis indexed by $I$
The basis vector at the distinguished index $i_0$ is constant one
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
A multi-index $a$ of length $n$ with values in $I$
